To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hydrodynamics and the area-to-volume constrain have a strong influence on domain coarsening, and that this can be understood in terms of an effective interfacial energy that includes the effects of hydrodynamic and area-to-volume forces.
the area-to-volum constraint has a strong effect on the domain growth dynamics of multicomponent fluid vesicles, and that hydrodynamic effects are important for the domain growth dynamics.

the dynamics of phase separation is strongly influenced by hydrodynamics and the area-to-volume ratio, that there are regimes of flat patches that grow, regimes that exhibit budding, and regimes that exhibit vesiculation, that the area-to volume constraint has a strong effect on crossovers, and that the dynamics of vesicle formation is very complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of domain growth in multicomponent vesicles, and the influence of hydrodynamic flow on this dynamics.
the investigation of the dynamics of phase separation of self-assembled fluid membranes in terms of the interplay of area-to-volume constraint and hydrodynamics.
the dynamics of phase separation and the dynamics of domain formation in fluid bilayer membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hydrodynamics has only little influence on the dynamics of phase separation, whereas the area-to-volume constraints have a strong effect.
hydrodynamic effects are of importance, but that they are not dominant in the dynamics of phase separation.

, in the absence of external fields, the dynamics of the domain growth in a fluid vesicle is determined solely by the interplay of the area-to-volume ratio and the interfacial tension, and that hydrodynamics has no significant effect on the domain growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the area constraint is crucial for the vesicle shape, and that the dynamics of the phase separation process can only be understood in a hydrodynamic framework.
the area-to-volum constraints and the hydrodynamics are crucial to the dynamics of phase separation.
the dynamics of the phase separation in the fluid vesicle system is strongly influenced by the presence of solvent particles and the area-to-volume constraints.

, in the presence of hydrodynamics, the domain dynamics of multicomponent fluid vesicles can be understood in terms of the dynamics of flat patches.
the dynamics of domain growth in fluid vesicles is very complex and cannot be reduced to simple analytical models.
